analysis.title: GS Dunn - GS US Daily Download 11 Nov 2026
key_insights: October CPI surprised to the upside across several categories, the third month of worse inflation news. GS expects a second 25bp hike in December and adds a third 25bp hike in March 2027.

A third hike could come in January, but GS thinks March is more likely because November and December inflation reports should be softer and larger start-of-year price increases should lift January inflation.

GS says oil futures have fallen substantially since the elections, so the bulk of energy-shock passthrough to consumer prices is behind us. GS remains confident inflation will be meaningfully lower by end-2027.
GS suspects most FOMC participants will signal a third hike in the December dot plot, and that a firmer January inflation report would make delivering it the path of least resistance.
GS left its terminal fed funds forecast unchanged at 3.25-3.5%. It now expects cuts to begin in December 2027 (previously September 2027), followed by cuts in March, June and September 2028.

Q3 earnings season so far: roughly half of S&P 500 firms discussed internal AI use cases, 13% quantified AI productivity impact on a specific use case, and 4% quantified the earnings impact. Both figures are up slightly from Q2.

GS Top of Mind covers the durability of the AI investment cycle, citing recent AI-related market stresses and new regulatory uncertainty. It features Chamath Palihapitiya, Eric Sheridan and Miriam Wheeler on who holds the risk and where AI ROI stands.

StubHub Q3: GMS and Adj. EBITDA ahead of Street, marketing leverage a source of upside, net leverage down to 2.5x from 4.5x at FY25 after $100mm of extra debt repayment and debt maturities extended to 2033. TTM FCF was $192mm, affected by the timing of World Cup-related buyer collections and seller payments.
GS reiterates Buy on StubHub (STUB) and lowers its 12-month PT to $9 from $11 after updating forward operating estimates.

Live Nation Investor Day: incremental AOI opportunities raised to $1,875M from $1,660M at the November 2025 Investor Day. Management's outlook implies about 11% annualized AOI growth to roughly $4,475M over the medium term, versus $4,481M consensus AOI for 2031E.

Live Nation Venue Nation is now a $925M AOI opportunity (vs $750M prior), driven by 38 large venues added through 2031 at 20%+ IRRs (vs 48 venues prior). Pre-opening costs are expected to rise about $40-50M YoY in 2027, with a similar step in 2028, and to peak in 2027-2028.

Live Nation sees a path to $6+ of Concerts AOI per fan over time, vs about $4.30-4.40 expected in 2026, driven by mix shift toward larger operated venues with more premium, food and beverage spending.

Live Nation's 7 recently opened international arenas and stadiums: 7M fans and $90M AOI in 2026, 9M run-rate fans and $190M run-rate AOI, 22% expected IRR, 14% expected yield and 13% 2026 pro rata yield.

Market update: October core CPI printed +30bps vs 20bps consensus with broad strength in components. Waller's overnight comments raised the possibility of larger moves after a warmer core print. The desk says the print likely locked in a 25bps December hike and one more in 1H27. The 10YR rose 10bps to 4.98%.

NVDA fell another ~6% on independent investigation, NYT reporting and a possible GOP House subpoena. The desk saw long supply and very little defense. AVGO (+3.8%) and AMD (+80bps) traded as primary beneficiaries of the NVDA news.

Ex-NVDA, volumes were light (SPX constituents tracking -15%). Floor activity was 5 on a 1-10 scale. Asset managers were moderate net sellers on large-cap tech supply, and HFs were net sellers with short > long, concentrated in tech and macro products.
Post-bell: CRWV +5% after Q3 revenue of $3.661b (vs guide $3.45b-$3.6b) and Q3 adjusted operating income of $379m (vs $200-$260m guide).
Calendar: Veterans Day, no major economic data releases. NYSE is open. SIFMA recommends bond markets stay closed.

market_movers.rationale: GS stays constructive on healthy demand, a more durable margin trajectory and improving balance sheet. It cut the 12-month PT to $9 from $11 after updating forward operating estimates.

CoreWeave (CRWV) post-bell Q3 (reported): revenue $3.661b vs guide $3.45b-$3.6b, adjusted operating income $379m vs guide $200-$260m. Shares +5% after hours.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Above the 20bps consensus with broad strength across components, which kept hike risk alive.
The print beat this consensus by 10bps.
GS added a third 25bp hike in March 2027. A January hike is possible.
Unchanged. GS now expects cuts to start in December 2027 instead of September 2027.
Up 10bps on the day after the CPI print, and rate-sensitive pockets of the market fell.
The source text prints '%110', which is likely a typo. The desk says the print likely locked in a 25bps December hike.

Recent AI-related market stresses and new regulatory uncertainty raise questions about AI investment cycle durability.

SPX constituent volumes tracking -15%, floor activity 5 on a 1-10 scale.

tension_points.bull_case: GS sees inflation falling meaningfully by end-2027 as tariff, energy-shock and AI price pressures fade, and oil futures have fallen since the elections.
tension_points.bear_case: Three straight months of worse inflation news and larger start-of-year price increases could lift January inflation and make a third hike the path of least resistance.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Softer November and December inflation reports would push the third hike to March rather than January, and the report says March is more likely than January.
